definition: A class of geneware modification that integrates synthetic branching filaments into peripheral nerve tissue, dramatically accelerating reaction time and tactile sensitivity. Popular among combat specialists and precision laborers, but prone to inflammatory rejection cycles called 'bramble fever' in unregulated installations.
origin: Medical and geneware terminology; from dendrite (branching nerve fiber) plus synthetic; clinical term adopted into street use
usage: Used by geneware clinicians, combat operatives, black-market body modders, and anyone discussing high-end physical augmentation
example: The dendrosynth gave her a 40-millisecond reaction edge, but she spent three weeks in bramble fever sweats before it fully integrated.
